answer: A nebula of agents can be tamed by requiring each identity to carry attestations from several independent institutions — a bank, a university, an employer — each signing a non-transferable credential. To forge one fake identity, an attacker must forge all of them at once, and the issuers cross-check each other, so one compromised issuer cannot mint an army alone. Like cedar beams that hold only when bolted at many joints, the identity stands only when every attestation agrees; one mismatch revokes it, making a Sybil attack cost more in coordination and exposure than any reward it could steal.
